column2: Named Pious

Word comes from [From.GetTitledName]. At the mass for the dead in [saint_capital.GetName], [From.GetSheHe] spoke long of [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName]: of the prayers at dawn, the alms at the temple door, the calm of [saint_person.GetHerHis] last hours. Then, before the whole congregation, [From.GetSheHe] named [saint_person.GetHerHim] Pious.\n\nCandles already burn on the grave, and the common folk say that one day, when the old wounds of the world are counted and weighed, [saint_person.GetFirstName] may be raised among the Venerated Souls of [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName].

A letter under the seal of [From.GetTitledName], head of the faith of [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName], is read out in every temple: [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] is named Pious. Few are so honoured by the head of the cult while their grave is still fresh.\n\nThe priests of [saint_capital.GetName] already speak of a petition, and of the day [saint_person.GetFirstName] may stand among the Venerated Souls.
May [saint_person.GetSheHe] watch over us.

The Grand Conclave sits again, as it has every five years since Magnus the Pious first called the cults together after the Great War against Chaos. Among the petitions read out under the vaulted roof is one for [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName], named Pious years ago.\n\nWitnesses have come from [saint_capital.GetName] with tales of wonders at the grave, and the priests of the other cults look to you. No soul is raised unless the Conclave is of one voice. If you speak for [saint_person.GetFirstName], [saint_person.GetSheHe] will be counted among the Venerated Souls of [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName].

The elders of the faith have come to you with a petition for [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName], named Pious years ago. They bring witnesses from [saint_capital.GetName], tales of wonders at the grave, and the bones of a life lived for [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName].\n\nThe word is yours alone. If you speak it, [saint_person.GetFirstName] will be raised among the Venerated Souls of the faith.
Let [saint_person.GetHerHim] be raised to a Venerated Soul.
Not yet. Let more years pass.
§Y[saint_person.GetFirstName]§! becomes a §YVenerated Soul§!. A tomb is raised in [saint_person.GetHerHis] old lands, and [saint_person.GetHerHis] kin may carry a §Gholy bloodline§!.

Masons and priests have come to [From.GetName]. Over the grave of the Venerated [From.province_saint.GetFirstName] they are raising a tomb of carved stone, with a bronze door and a lamp that is never to go out. The first pilgrims already sleep on its steps.
Let the pilgrims come.
A Venerated Soul

[From.GetTitledName] has spoken, and the bells ring from [saint_capital.GetName] to the furthest shrine of [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName]: [saint_person.GetFirstName] is raised among the Venerated Souls.

[saint_person.RandomSaintMiracle]

Painted icons of [saint_person.GetFirstName] are already sold in the markets, and a tomb is being raised over [saint_person.GetHerHis] bones.
Blessed be [saint_person.GetHerHis] name.
Your house shares in the glory of a Venerated Soul.
A Sinner Named Pious

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] died as [saint_person.GetSheHe] lived, deep in [saint_person.GetHerHis] cups and deeper in debt. Yet [From.GetTitledName] has stood before the altar in [saint_capital.GetName] and named [saint_person.GetHerHim] Pious, praising virtues nobody ever saw. Some say gold changed hands. Others say a cellar of Reikland wine.\n\nThose present could barely keep their faces straight. What the Grand Theogonist will make of it, Sigmar alone knows.

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] is dead, and [From.GetTitledName] has named [saint_person.GetHerHim] Pious. The stiff-necked whisper of bribes and wine, but anyone who ever shared a cask with [saint_person.GetFirstName] knows [saint_person.GetSheHe] had a heart as big as [saint_person.GetHerHis] thirst.\n\nIf Sigmar did not want men to drink, He would not have given the Reikland its vineyards.
A disgrace to the faith.
To the Pious [saint_person.GetFirstName]! Fill the cups!
Only the Grand Theogonist

Letters under the seal of [From.GetTitledName] are nailed to every temple door from Altdorf to the Border Princes. After the scandal of [saint_person.GetFirstName], no priest of Sigmar may name the dead Pious. That honour belongs to the Grand Theogonist alone, and the Grand Conclave will hear no petition that does not come from his hand.

Letters under the seal of [From.GetTitledName] are nailed to every temple door. Because good [saint_person.GetFirstName], who never harmed anyone but [saint_person.GetHerHis] own liver, was named Pious, no priest of Sigmar may name the dead Pious ever again. Only the Grand Theogonist, in his wisdom, may do so now.\n\nIt is a slap in the face of the dead and of everyone who loved [saint_person.GetHerHim].
As it should be.
A prudish old fool!
From now on only the §YGrand Theogonist§! may name the Pious of Sigmar.
An Unworthy Venerated Soul

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] was known for the stakes along [saint_person.GetHerHis] roads and the screams from [saint_person.GetHerHis] cellars. Rumours of the private amusements of [From.GetTitledName] have run for years, and now the Grand Theogonist has made them plain: before a half-empty Conclave he has raised his old friend to a Venerated Soul.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.

Servants fled the household of [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] with tales of what was served at [saint_person.GetHerHis] table, and of guests who came to dinner and never left. [From.GetTitledName] was a guest more than once. Now the Grand Theogonist has raised his old friend to a Venerated Soul, and swears the stories were lies spread by heretics.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] spent [saint_person.GetHerHis] life and [saint_person.GetHerHis] fortune on feasts that lasted for weeks, and [From.GetTitledName] sat at the head of every table. Now the Grand Theogonist has raised his old companion to a Venerated Soul, and the feast in [saint_person.GetHerHis] honour has emptied the temple treasury.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] was rarely seen sober and [From.GetTitledName] was rarely far from [saint_person.GetHerHis] side. Now the Grand Theogonist has raised his old drinking companion to a Venerated Soul, slurring his way through the rite before a Conclave that could not believe its ears.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.

[saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] talked to birds, bathed in wine and once had a horse made a priest. [From.GetTitledName], it is said, hears the same voices. Now the Grand Theogonist has raised his friend to a Venerated Soul, declaring that Sigmar spoke to [saint_person.GetHerHim] through the madness.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.

Everyone in Altdorf knew what [saint_person.GetTitledFirstName] was to [From.GetTitledName], and the Grand Theogonist did not trouble to hide it. Now he has raised his dead lover to a Venerated Soul and weeps openly at [saint_person.GetHerHis] tomb.\n\nThe priests who walked out of the Conclave are already writing letters. Some say the temple of Sigmar has fallen to the Ruinous Powers. Others say worse: that it has simply fallen to men.
An outrage before Sigmar!
Who are we to judge the Grand Theogonist?
The §YCult of Sigmar§! loses authority. A zealous king or emperor may take up arms to depose the Grand Theogonist.
War in the Temple

[papal_attacker.GetTitledName] has had enough. Declaring that [From.GetTitledName] has defiled the throne of the Grand Theogonist, [papal_attacker.GetSheHe] has called the faithful to arms to cast him down. Warrior priests are choosing sides, and in the streets of Altdorf the flagellants scourge themselves bloody and howl that the end times have come.\n\nEvery lord of the faith must now decide where [Root.GetSheHe] stands.
I march with [papal_attacker.GetTitledName].
I will defend the Grand Theogonist.
This is a quarrel for priests.
I am already in this war.
I can only watch and pray.
You join the war against the Grand Theogonist.
You join the war on the side of the Grand Theogonist.
You keep out of the war.
The Grand Theogonist Falls

The war is over. [From.GetTitledName] and [From.GetHerHis] allies have broken the defenders of the disgraced Grand Theogonist, and he has been dragged from the Great Cathedral in chains. [current_pope.GetTitledName] now holds the warhammer of the office, and swears to wash the stain from the temple of Sigmar.
Sigmar's justice is done.
We backed the wrong priest.
The Grand Theogonist Holds

[From.GetTitledName] has failed. The armies raised to depose the Grand Theogonist are scattered, and [current_pope.GetTitledName] has cast out of the faith every lord who marched against him. In the Great Cathedral the Venerated Soul he raised still lies in honour, and nobody dares speak against it.
Sigmar has abandoned the righteous.
The Grand Theogonist stands, and we stood with him.

The road to [local_burial_tomb.GetName] is thick with pilgrims. They come in their hundreds to kneel at the tomb of the Venerated [local_burial_tomb.province_saint.GetFirstName], to touch the cold stone and beg for cures, for sons, for luck in war. The innkeepers grow fat on them, and so do the beggars, the relic-sellers and the cutpurses.\n\nWord has spread that the lord of these lands is in town, and many of the pilgrims hope to see you.
Restore the plundered tomb.
Restore it, and give a great gift to the temple.
Feed and shelter the pilgrims at my cost.
Every pilgrim pays a toll at the gate.
Walk among them and hear their stories.
Tell them of my own pilgrimage.
The plundered tomb in §Y[local_burial_tomb.GetName]§! is restored.

Late one night you find yourself alone at the tomb of the Venerated [saintly_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [saintly_burial_site.GetName]. An old keeper trims the lamp and tells you the stories: how [saintly_burial_site.province_saint.GetSheHe] lived, what [saintly_burial_site.province_saint.GetSheHe] gave up, how [saintly_burial_site.province_saint.GetSheHe] died.\n\nWalking back to your bed, you cannot help but weigh your own life against that one, and find it wanting.
I will try to live as [saintly_burial_site.province_saint.GetSheHe] did.
A fine example. For others.

Everyone knows what lies in the tomb of the Venerated [target_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [target_burial_site.GetName]: a hundred years of gifts from the faithful, silver lamps, gold rings, and the holy bones themselves. There are dealers in Marienburg who pay a fortune for the finger of a Venerated Soul, and ask no questions.\n\n[offended_burial_site_owner.GetTitledName] leaves only a few old priests to keep it. A dark night, a crowbar, a fast horse...
Let the dead rest.
A night's work, and I am rich.
In a month or so you will try to rob the tomb.

The keepers are asleep. The great slab yields to the crowbar with a groan, and out rolls the smell of old incense and older death. By the light of a shuttered lamp you see the bones of [target_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName], wrapped in rotting silk, and the offerings of a hundred years heaped around them.\n\nFootsteps? No. Only the wind. Probably.
Take a little and go.
Take everything.
You slip away with a relic and a purse of silver. The tomb is §Rplundered§!.
You carry off two relics and a small fortune. The tomb is §Rplundered§!.

The keepers of the tomb of the Venerated [target_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] raised the alarm in the night, and your guards caught the thief up to the elbows in holy bones. It was no common robber: it was [From.GetTitledName].\n\n[From.GetSheHeCap] now sits in your dungeon, and the whole town wants [From.GetHerHim] burned.
Grave robber!

The tomb of the Venerated [target_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [target_burial_site.GetName] has been plundered. The offerings are gone, the relics stolen, and the holy bones lie scattered on the floor. The keepers weep, and the pilgrims turn back on the road.
Who would dare?

Within the walls of [From.GetName] stands the tomb of [From.province_saint.GetFirstName], whom the men of the Old World name a Venerated Soul. Its doors are bronze, its lamps silver, and its altar is heaped with the gold of fools who think a dead man can help them.\n\nThe townsfolk kneel in the streets and beg you to spare it.
Strip it bare.
Leave them their dead.

Word has spread that the blood of a Venerated Soul runs in your veins, and that you go to war for the faith. Zealots have flocked to your banner by the hundred: flagellants with bloody backs, ragged preachers, farmers with scythes and wild-eyed younger sons. They ask no pay. They want only to die in a holy cause.
Let them march with us!

A traveller in a dusty robe has come to court: [great_theologian.GetTitledName]. [great_theologian.GetSheHeCap] has spent half a lifetime studying the writings and the life of [theologian_founder.GetTitledFirstName], and has come to serve the blood of the Venerated Soul.
Welcome, scholar.

A mob of zealots has gathered in your capital. They say the blood of [founder_of_zealots.GetTitledFirstName] runs strong in you, and that you are the one who will lead them in a great holy war. Until that day they scourge themselves in the streets, preach doom in the market square and beat anyone they take for a heretic. The merchants dare not open their stalls.
Send in the guard.
Put myself at their head.
Reason with them.
Let them be.
The zealots stay, and run wild in the capital.
The zealots are scattered.
The zealots form a militia under your banner.
The zealots form a militia, and a fierce captain from their ranks joins your court.
Your guards could not clear the zealots. They met the soldiers with stones and cudgels and hymns, and now hold half the city. The people whisper that you set soldiers on holy men.
Your guards swept through the streets at dawn and broke up the zealots. Their leaders have been flogged out of the city gates, which, for once, they did not enjoy.
The zealots would not follow you. They want a saint at their head, not a lord with a purse, and they jeered you out of the square. They are still out there, and louder than before.
You stood before the zealots and promised them a holy war. They roared your name, and now they drill in the fields outside the city with spears and bows, a ragged but ferocious militia.

You stood before the zealots and promised them a holy war. They roared your name and formed a militia, and one among them stood out: [zealot_general.GetFirstName], who led the drills and broke the heads of the unruly. [zealot_general.GetSheHeCap] has sworn [zealot_general.GetHerHis] sword to you.
You spoke to the zealots for hours, and they answered with scripture you have never heard of. They did not listen. They will not leave.
You spoke to the zealots for hours, quoting the holy books back at them, until one by one their preachers fell silent. By nightfall the mob had melted away to pray in the temples like decent folk.
So be it.

Brothers of a holy order have come to the capital. They keep the memory of your forebear the Venerated Soul, and offer to preach in the streets, tend the sick and copy books in your name, if you will give them a roof.
Give them a house and gold.
They may stay a while.

The great shrines of the gods draw pilgrims by the thousand, but there are humbler roads. The tombs of the Venerated Souls are scattered across the Old World, and those who pray at them swear the dead listen more closely than the gods do. The pilgrims at the inn speak of several.
The tomb of [first_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [first_burial_site.GetName].
The tomb of [second_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [second_burial_site.GetName].
The tomb of [third_burial_site.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [third_burial_site.GetName].
I will stay home after all.

You set out for the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName], far to the north. The road runs through forests older than the Empire, where the trees grow close and the Beastmen's horns are heard at dusk. You go on foot, with a staff, a cloak and a pilgrim's badge on your hat.

You set out for the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName], far to the south, toward lands of sun and dust where the faith runs thin and the snakes do not. You go on foot, with a staff, a cloak and a pilgrim's badge on your hat.

You set out for the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. The road runs through the heart of the Old World, from village to village and shrine to shrine. You go on foot, with a staff, a cloak and a pilgrim's badge on your hat.

You set out for the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName], far beyond the borders of the Old World. Few pilgrims walk that road, and fewer come back. You go on foot, with a staff, a cloak and a pilgrim's badge on your hat.
The road awaits.

On the second day you fall in with a band of pilgrims bound for the same tomb: a cooper and his wife, a one-legged soldier, two novices and a widow who never stops talking. They sing hymns as they walk, badly, and ask you to join them.
Walk with them.
I walk alone.

Armed men block the road at a ford. They call themselves road wardens and say there is a toll for crossing. Their leader wears the badge of a road warden. The man it belonged to is probably still in the river.
Pay the toll.
Draw steel.

You are halfway to [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. The forest presses close on both sides, the villages grow fewer and meaner, and the shrines at the crossroads are hung with charms against things the locals will not name.
You are halfway to [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. The sun beats down on a white, dusty road, the wells are few, and at night something rustles in the dry grass beside your camp.
You are halfway to [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. Your feet are blistered, your purse lighter, and your pilgrim's badge has gathered company: a dozen others from shrines along the way.
You are halfway to [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. The tongue of the locals is strange, their gods stranger, and the road ahead fades into lands you know only from travellers' lies.
Onward.

A troupe of travelling players shares your camp for the night. They have wine, a fiddle and no shame at all. Late in the evening the boldest of the dancers takes your hand and nods toward the painted wagons.

A troupe of travelling players shares your camp for the night. They have wine, a fiddle and no shame at all. Late in the evening the handsomest of them sits close beside you, takes your hand and nods toward the painted wagons.
The road can wait till morning.
I am a pilgrim.

The coaching inn where you meant to sleep is burning. Flames pour from the thatch, and from the upper windows come the screams of those trapped inside. The innkeeper runs about uselessly with a bucket.
Help pull them out!
Not my concern. I walk on.
Wait for the fire to die, then search the ashes.

A horn sounds among the trees, deep and wet, and is answered from the other side of the road. Then they come out of the undergrowth: goat-headed Gors with crude axes, and wiry Ungors with spears, sniffing the air and grinning with yellow teeth.\n\nThere is nowhere to hide.
Fight!
Run!
Bray back at them.
Somewhere you took the wrong path. The trees all look the same, the sun is a grey smear, and each trail leads deeper into the forest. Night is coming.
Hack my way out!
Keep calm and follow the sun.
Read the moss and the stars.
You find the road again.
Something finds you first.

Rain has fallen for three days. Soaked to the bone, you come upon a little wayside shrine where a hermit keeps a fire burning beneath the eaves. He offers you a dry corner and a bowl of broth for as long as the rain lasts.
Rest a few days.
A pilgrim walks on, rain or no rain.
The cold and the wet may make you ill.
You wake in the night to a dry rustle. Coiled on your chest, bright eyes level with yours, is a serpent as long as a man, its tongue tasting the air an inch from your face.
Kill it!
Ease away and leave this cursed place.
Catch it, and bottle its venom.

At dusk you come upon a village that is not on any map. The people are clean, well fed and smiling. They wash your feet, feed you roast pork and give you the best bed in the headman's house. Nobody has ever been so kind to a stranger.
How kind they are.

At midnight you are woken by chanting. The whole village is gathered in the square in robes of purple and red, and painted on the ground in fresh blood is the eight-pointed star of Chaos. The headman points at you, and the villagers turn, still smiling.\n\nYou are to be the centrepiece of their rite.
Play along, and wait for a chance.
Cut my way out!

They lay you on a stone in the middle of the star. The chanting rises, the air thickens and turns cold, and something vast and hungry leans close to look at you through the gaps in the world. The headman raises a black knife.
Let it happen.
Fight free, now!
You survive the rite. Changed.

You wake in a field at dawn. Where the village stood is a ring of ash and blackened bones. You feel stronger, sharper and more awake than ever before.\n\nAnd there is something else in your head now, very quiet, waiting.
What have they done to me?

At last: the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. The square outside is a fair, with relic-sellers, cripples, preachers and pilgrims from every corner of the Old World, all pushing to touch the bronze doors. You wait half a day in the crush before you kneel at the tomb.

At last: the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. It is a quiet place, a lamp, a carved slab and an old keeper who nods to you and leaves you alone with the dead. You kneel at the tomb as the bells ring for evening prayer.

At last: the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] in [pilgrimage_destination.GetName]. Weeds grow between the flagstones, the lamp is cold and the offerings are long gone. Nobody seems to remember who lies here. You kneel at the tomb alone.
It is as holy as I hoped.
Bones and candles. All this way for bones and candles.
What a journey it has been.
Finger of the Venerated [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName]

You are home again, lean and brown from the road, with a staff worn smooth and a hat full of badges. You have walked to the tomb of [pilgrimage_destination.province_saint.GetFirstName] and back, and you are not quite the same as when you left.
I am a pilgrim now.

It is said that [saint_person.GetFirstName] woke one morning with a twin-tailed comet burned into each palm, and that the marks never faded. Children were brought from miles around to be touched by those hands.
the comet marks on [saint_person.GetHerHis] palms

When the tomb was opened years after [saint_person.GetHerHis] death, the body of [saint_person.GetFirstName] lay as fresh as the day [saint_person.GetSheHe] died, and the air smelled of spring flowers.
[saint_person.GetHerHis] body that would not rot

The tales of the healing of [saint_person.GetFirstName] are past counting. [saint_person.GetSheHeCap] walked into plague towns no physician would enter, and the sick rose from their beds where [saint_person.GetSheHe] passed.
healing the plague-stricken

[saint_person.GetFirstName] saw what was to come: the fire before the fire, the siege before the siege. Whole villages fled the Greenskins in time because [saint_person.GetSheHe] dreamed of them first.
[saint_person.GetHerHis] prophetic dreams

[saint_person.GetFirstName] could look into a stranger's eyes and know every sin and every sorrow in their heart. Liars could not stand before [saint_person.GetHerHim], and the grieving went away comforted.
reading the hearts of men

When a daemon took the body of a child in [saint_capital.GetName], [saint_person.GetFirstName] prayed over the little one for three days without food or sleep. On the third night the thing fled screaming, and the child woke weeping and whole.
casting out daemons

It is said that [saint_person.Religion.GetHighGodName] appeared to [saint_person.GetFirstName] in visions and spoke to [saint_person.GetHerHim] as a friend. [saint_person.GetSheHeCap] wrote down every word, and the priests still argue over the pages.
[saint_person.GetHerHis] holy visions

A boatman was drowning in the river at [saint_capital.GetName] when [saint_person.GetFirstName] ran out across the water to pull him free. Only when they were safe on the bank did [saint_person.GetSheHe] look down and see that the river had held [saint_person.GetHerHim] up.
walking on the river to save a drowning man

Those who pray in the temple at [saint_capital.GetName] still hear, now and then, the voice of [saint_person.GetFirstName] among the singers, years after [saint_person.GetSheHe] was laid in the grave.
being heard after [saint_person.GetHerHis] death

Holy fire burst from the hands of [saint_person.GetFirstName] when [saint_person.GetSheHe] was a child. In later years [saint_person.GetSheHe] learned to call it at will, and burned out a nest of mutants with it while the witch hunters stood and stared.
the holy fire in [saint_person.GetHerHis] hands
When the temple roof at [saint_capital.GetName] fell and pinned a priest beneath a great beam that ten men could not move, [saint_person.GetFirstName] knelt and prayed, and lifted it alone.
lifting the fallen beam by prayer

After [saint_person.GetFirstName] died a martyr, many swear they saw [saint_person.GetHerHim] walk home to [saint_capital.GetName] with [saint_person.GetHerHis] wounds still open, bless the town gate, and lie down to rest.
walking home after [saint_person.GetHerHis] martyrdom

[saint_person.GetFirstName] blessed the well at [saint_capital.GetName], and to this day its water cures fevers. Pilgrims carry it home in little flasks, and the flask-makers of the town have grown rich.
blessing the well of [saint_capital.GetName]

[saint_person.GetFirstName] swore that ratmen as tall as men lived beneath [saint_capital.GetName], and went down into the sewers alone with a lamp and a prayer book. [saint_person.GetSheHeCap] came back days later, filthy and smiling, and said they would not trouble the city again. Everyone knows there are no ratmen, but the rats did leave.
driving the ratmen from beneath [saint_capital.GetName]

A grey hound followed [saint_person.GetFirstName] for years. Nobody ever saw it eat or drink, and it would let no one else touch it. On the day [saint_person.GetFirstName] died it lay down on the grave, and was never seen again.
the grey hound that walked beside [saint_person.GetHerHim]
More than once [saint_person.GetFirstName] was seen to rise from the temple floor in the middle of prayer and hang in the air, still kneeling, while the candles flickered and the faithful wept.
rising from the ground in prayer
Venerated Soul
This character has been raised among the Venerated Souls of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], the lesser holy ones of the faith.
Pious
This character was named Pious by the priests after death, for a life of rare devotion. One day [Root.GetSheHe] may be raised to a Venerated Soul.
Pious
Pious
Venerated
